title: Descent of a fixed ordinary scalar and signed-line comparison
statement: Let $X,R,S,\alpha,p,L,K$ be as in [def-pur-ordinary-line-scalar-data], and let $l,k$ be line data for $L,K$. Suppose given ordinary natural isomorphisms $o_m:E_pT_{L,m}\cong T_{K,m}E_p$ for every integer $m$. There are derived natural isomorphisms $d_m:D_pF_{L,m}\cong F_{K,m}D_p$ such that, on every flat-term K-flat complex $P$, the composite of $d_m(Q_RP)$, $F_{K,m}(\operatorname{compute}_p P)$ and the target line-factor comparison at $E_pP$ equals $D_p(l_m(P))$, followed by $\operatorname{compute}_p(T_{L,m}P)$ and $Q_S(o_m(P))$. All maps are the fixed quotient, line-factor and ordinary-comparison maps of [def-pur-ordinary-line-scalar-data]. This assertion requires no evaluation compatibility or normalization of the ordinary signed-power comparison.

proof.text: Restrict cochain complexes to flat-term K-flat objects. A flat-term K-flat resolution supplies a representative of every homotopy object and refines roofs. The resolving representative localization and full quotient imply that precomposition with this representative functor is fully faithful.

The universal scalar counit is invertible on these representatives. Whisker the source line-factor isomorphism, the scalar computation on the tensor representative, the ordinary cochain comparison, the inverse target line factor, and the inverse scalar computation. Line flatness ensures the tensor representative is still in the resolving class.

Take the inverse image of this natural isomorphism under fully faithful precomposition. Its map-preimage equality gives the displayed representative square by cancelling the computation and line-factor inverse maps.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinary_scalar_line_flat_descent
    (α : R ⟶ S) (p : SuccessiveDerivedQuotient.Presentation.{t + 1, t, max a (t + 1), w}
      (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology X) α)
    (L : Modules.{t, a} X R) (K : Modules.{t, a} X S)
    (l : LineData L) (k : LineData K)
    (o : ∀ m : ℤ, tensor.{t, a} L m ⋙ p.ordinary ≅
      p.ordinary ⋙ tensor.{t, a} K m) :
    ∃ d : ∀ m : ℤ, twist.{t, a, w} L m ⋙ p.derived ≅
        p.derived ⋙ twist.{t, a, w} K m,
      ∀ (m : ℤ) (P : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, a} X R) ℤ), FlatModel P →
        (d m).hom.app (𝒬[R].obj P) ≫
          (twist.{t, a, w} K m).map (compute.{t, a, w} p P) ≫
          (k.factors m).hom.app ((p.ordinary.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
        p.derived.map ((l.factors m).hom.app P) ≫
          compute.{t, a, w} p (((tensor.{t, a} L m).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
          𝒬[S].map
            ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso (o m) (.up ℤ)).hom.app P)
